primary_claim: An apparent 'typo uplift' where Claude Haiku's accuracy rose as typo rate increased on BigCodeBench was an artifact of the grading harness only extracting the last code block, not a genuine capability increase; once all code blocks are accounted for, the accuracy increase disappears.

effect.value: Haiku 4.5 rose from 51.2% to 71.1% (+19.9pp) as typo rate rose from 0% to 16%; Opus 4.5 fell from 82.0% to 72.7% (-9.3pp); after fixing the grading harness to account for all code blocks, the uplift disappears

contradicts_or_qualifies: Their own initial hypothesis that typos increase effort/accuracy the way difficult fonts aid human retention
quote: The initial observation of accuracy uplift was due to a output formatting behavior shift that gradually aligns with the grader, not an actual capability increase.
